chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fasts a fast that he has appointed upon himself, or who fasts the sacred months, and a month or two pass without him making it up. He said: He does not fast during travel, and he does not make up anything from voluntary fasting except the three days that he used to fast every month, and he does not make them equivalent to the obligatory fast, unless I love for you to persist in good deeds. He said: And the one who fasts the sacred months, it suffices him to fast three days in place of each month of the sacred months.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up missed voluntary fasts while traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Isfār clarifies the distinction between *nadb* (voluntary) and *wājib* (obligatory) fasting, establishing that missed voluntary days do not require strict compensation (*qadā*) unless they were habitual acts of devotion. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining spiritual continuity (*dawām*) by preserving specific monthly fasts even during travel, while offering flexibility for general voluntary fasting. The ruling underscores the principle that voluntary acts, unlike obligatory ones, are not strictly bound by rigid makeup requirements when interrupted by travel or other factors.
